problem:
The defect WO-0008 was raised to fix exists unchanged in two other Core types, and in one of them it hangs the process rather than corrupting a number. WaveScheduler.Tick and PlayerMotor.Tick carry the identical guard `if (dt < 0f) throw` with the identical message 'dt must be >= 0.' -- the same mismatched predicate, character for character, that PRO-0002 documented in RunState. Both are fed Time.deltaTime directly from the Unity shell. Fixing RunState alone leaves the class of defect in place and leaves the studio believing it was closed.

WaveScheduler is the severe one. Assets/Core/Spawning/WaveScheduler.cs:60-78: a non-finite dt passes the guard, then `_timeUntilNextSpawn -= dt` at line 70, then `while (_timeUntilNextSpawn <= 0f)` at line 73. With dt = float.PositiveInfinity, _timeUntilNextSpawn becomes -Infinity; the loop condition holds; each iteration appends a SpawnRequest to the caller's list and executes `_timeUntilNextSpawn += _interval`, and -Infinity plus any finite interval is still -Infinity. The loop cannot terminate. It spawns enemies into the caller's buffer until the process exhausts memory. That is not a silent wrong number, it is a hang plus an unbounded allocation, and it is reachable from Assets/Unity/EnemySpawner.cs:45 on any frame that produces a non-finite delta. With dt = float.NaN the same line makes _timeUntilNextSpawn NaN, `NaN <= 0f` is false, and the scheduler silently never spawns again for the rest of the run -- absorbing and unrecoverable, exactly like ElapsedSeconds.

PlayerMotor is the quieter one and its failure mode is arguably worse for a player. Assets/Core/Player/PlayerMotor.cs:44-64: dt = NaN makes PositionX NaN through the Clamp at line 58 (Clamp at line 89 tests `x < _minX` then presumably `x > _maxX`, both false for NaN, so NaN is returned unchanged and the player leaves the world), and makes _fireCooldown NaN at line 60, where `if (_fireCooldown < 0f)` is false so the NaN is retained. Then TryFire at line 80 tests `if (_fireCooldown > 0f) return false` -- false for NaN -- so the weapon fires on every single call, permanently, at unbounded rate. One non-finite frame converts the motor into an infinite-fire-rate cheat that no exception, flag or test reports.

Neither type has any non-finite dt test. Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/WaveSchedulerTests.cs and PlayerMotorTests.cs contain 9 tests each and none passes a non-finite dt, so both suites are green over both defects. WO-0008's twelve criteria are scoped entirely to Assets/Core/Run/RunState.cs and say nothing about either file, so this is not a failure against WO-0008 and I am filing no challenge against its implementer.
evidence: Assets/Core/Spawning/WaveScheduler.cs:60-63 -- `if (dt < 0f) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(dt), dt, "dt must be >= 0.")`, the same predicate/message mismatch PRO-0002 documented in RunState

Assets/Core/Spawning/WaveScheduler.cs:70-78 -- `_timeUntilNextSpawn -= dt` followed by `while (_timeUntilNextSpawn <= 0f) { into.Add(...); _timeUntilNextSpawn += _interval; }`; for dt = +Infinity the accumulator is -Infinity and `-Infinity + _interval` is -Infinity, so the loop never terminates and `into` grows without bound
Assets/Core/Player/PlayerMotor.cs:44-47 -- the identical `dt < 0f` guard and identical message
Assets/Core/Player/PlayerMotor.cs:58-64 and 72-87 -- dt = NaN poisons _fireCooldown, and TryFire's `if (_fireCooldown > 0f) return false` is false for NaN, so every subsequent TryFire returns true

Assets/Unity/EnemySpawner.cs:45 -- `_scheduler.Tick(Time.deltaTime, _pending)` and Assets/Unity/PlayerController.cs:33 -- `_motor.Tick(Time.deltaTime, Input.GetAxisRaw("Horizontal"))`; both feed the shell's delta straight into the defective guards

Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/WaveSchedulerTests.cs and Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/PlayerMotorTests.cs -- 9 [Test] methods each, no non-finite dt case in either; a grep for NaN, Infinity or IsFinite returns nothing in either file
proposedWork:
One L3 work order to engineering, scoped to Assets/Core/Spawning/**, Assets/Core/Player/** and Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/**, applying the guard RunState now has -- reject dt whenever `float.IsFinite(dt)` is false or `dt < 0f` -- to WaveScheduler.Tick and PlayerMotor.Tick, with a message that states the predicate actually enforced, exactly as WO-0008 criterion 12 required for RunState. No authorisation to invert an existing assertion is needed this time: I checked, and neither suite has a test that would change verdict, because neither ever passes a non-finite dt. That is the whole problem.

Regression tests, each of which must be shown failing against the unmodified code and passing after: WaveScheduler.Tick(float.PositiveInfinity, buffer) throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException and appends nothing -- this test must be written with a bounded buffer or a timeout, because against today's code it does not fail, it hangs, and a hanging test in CI is a worse outcome than a red one. WaveScheduler.Tick(float.NaN, buffer) throws, appends nothing, and a subsequent valid Tick still spawns on schedule. PlayerMotor.Tick(float.NaN, 0f) throws and leaves PositionX and FireCooldown finite and unchanged, and a subsequent TryFire still respects the cooldown. Same three shapes for NegativeInfinity.

The work order should also state the invariant as a type-wide rule rather than three separate fixes, since it is now the third instance: every Core method taking a dt parameter rejects any dt that is not a finite non-negative number, and its message names that predicate. That is a candidate for promotion out of prose into a test or analyzer per the lessons process.
expectedBenefit: Closes an unbounded-allocation hang that is reachable from a single frame of the shipped Unity shell, and an unbounded fire-rate exploit that no exception or flag reports. More importantly it prevents WO-0008 from being recorded as having closed a defect class when it closed one of three instances: RunState was the instance that happened to be read, not the worst one. The severe case here is strictly worse than PRO-0002's -- a poisoned clock still lets the game run, an infinite loop does not.
